OCEAN.behavior.label: Ocean Water
OCEAN.behavior.hint: Fill this Region with procedural, interactive ocean water.
OCEAN.beach.label: Beach
OCEAN.beach.hint: Fill this Region with a procedural sandy beach. Where it overlaps an Ocean Region is the shoreline.
OCEAN.beachFields.sandScale.label: Sand Tiling (px)
OCEAN.beachFields.sandScale.hint: World pixels per sand texture tile; smaller = finer grain.
OCEAN.beachFields.edgeSoftness.label: Edge Softness
OCEAN.beachFields.edgeSoftness.hint: How softly the beach Region outline fades.
OCEAN.beachFields.elevation.label: Elevation
OCEAN.beachFields.elevation.hint: Render elevation; beaches sit below water.
OCEAN.fields.preset.label: Water Style
OCEAN.fields.preset.hint: Preset that defines the color and look of the water.
OCEAN.fields.intensity.label: Wave Intensity
OCEAN.fields.intensity.hint: Overall strength of the waves and surface motion (0 = calm, 2 = stormy).
OCEAN.fields.windAngle.label: Wind Direction
OCEAN.fields.windAngle.hint: Controls the direction of FFT wave travel and whitecap layout, in degrees.
OCEAN.fields.flowSpeed.label: Flow Speed
OCEAN.fields.flowSpeed.hint: Speed the whole surface drifts along the wind direction (0 = no flow, higher = faster), like a river or current.
OCEAN.fields.underwaterOpacity.label: Underwater Murk
OCEAN.fields.underwaterOpacity.hint: Controls underwater tint and absorption without fading surface foam.
OCEAN.fields.waterDepth.label: Water Depth
OCEAN.fields.waterDepth.hint: Overall depth: deeper = darker water and less see-through; shallower = lighter water and a more visible map below.
OCEAN.fields.elevation.label: Render Elevation
OCEAN.fields.elevation.hint: Elevation at which the water surface is drawn. Tokens above this elevation appear on top of the water.
OCEAN.lightEditor.adaptiveHint: When switching light moods, automatically adapts some reflection values (e.g. crest translucency is halved at sunset / moonlight).
OCEAN.lightEditor.dragHint: Drag the sun on the canvas to move the key light; drag the ring handle to resize the lit area.
OCEAN.lightEditor.canvasNotReady: The canvas is not ready yet, so Ocean light cannot be edited.
OCEAN.settings.quality.label: Regular Scene Water · Quality
OCEAN.settings.quality.hint: Affects only Region water in regular Scenes, not full-screen 3D sea travel. Performance runs more smoothly; Quality keeps more wave and interaction detail. Use 3D Sea Travel Settings on this page for travel quality.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.label: 3D Sea Travel · Quality
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.hint: Affects only full-screen 3D sea travel on this device, not water in regular Scenes. Low, Medium, and High adjust clouds, render resolution, reflections, and antialiasing without changing tiers automatically.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.localNote: The GM sets world defaults for quality and mouse parallax. You can follow those defaults or override them only on this device. Regular Scene water is unaffected.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.legacyNote: This device is still using a legacy tier. It will stay unchanged until you select and save Low, Medium, or High here.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.low.label: Low
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.low.recomme: Best for older gaming laptops, entry-level dedicated graphics, or stronger integrated graphics at 1080p.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.medium.reco: Best for mainstream gaming laptops and desktops. Recommended for most players.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.high.label: High
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.high.summar: Keeps the full cloud, reflection, and antialiasing presentation.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.high.recomm: Best for mid-to-high-end gaming PCs or players who want the full presentation at higher resolutions.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.saved: 3D sea travel settings saved on this device.
OCEAN.settings.travelQuality.saveFailed: Could not save 3D sea travel settings: {message}
OCEAN.settings.quickStart.hint: Review regular water, travel scenes, the Scenic3D dependency, and personal quality settings. This remains available after choosing never to show the guide automatically.
OCEAN.settings.travelMouseParallax.label: Mouse Parallax
OCEAN.settings.travelMouseParallax.hint: When enabled, moving the mouse gently offsets the current 3D travel shot without intercepting Foundry UI input.
OCEAN.settings.tokenWake.label: Regular Scene Water · Token Wakes
OCEAN.settings.tokenWake.hint: Affects only water in regular Scenes. Tokens moving across the water leave a trailing wake of ripples.
OCEAN.settings.persistWakeSpeed.label: Regular Scene Water · 3D Ship Wake Speed
OCEAN.settings.persistWakeSpeed.hint: Affects Scenic3D ships in regular Scenes. With Persistent Wake enabled, this controls how fast the trail flows behind the ship. Lower is slower.
OCEAN.settings.debugTools.label: Debug Tools
OCEAN.settings.debugTools.hint: Show author-facing tuning entries (e.g. the per-ship wake button on the 3D ship HUD). Keep off for normal play.
OCEAN.hud.persistentWake: Persistent Wake (on = always trails behind the ship, independent from the water; off = only while moving)
OCEAN.shipWake.title: Ship Wake · Per-Ship
OCEAN.shipWake.hint: Changes apply to this ship only and are stored on the token. Untouched parameters keep following the global / hull defaults, so global tweaks still reach this ship. Drag to preview live; release to save.
OCEAN.shipWake.bakeHint: Bake this ship's customizations into the default for its hull model: every ship of this model (including future ones) uses it, and this ship's per-ship overrides are cleared.
OCEAN.shipWake.baked: Saved as hull default — all ships of this model updated.
OCEAN.warning.fftUnsupported: This browser/GPU does not support Ocean FFT water, so true whitecaps could not be enabled.
OCEAN.settings.rippleResolution.label: Ripple Resolution
OCEAN.settings.rippleResolution.hint: Resolution of the interactive ripple simulation. Higher is sharper but heavier.
OCEAN.debug.title: Ocean Debug Panel
OCEAN.studio.title: Ocean Studio
OCEAN.debug.notReady: Ocean debug is not ready yet.
OCEAN.capture.title: Ocean Capture Checklist
OCEAN.capture.hint: Use the same camera and switch through each item before taking screenshots. Copy the macro command into a Foundry macro for long-term use.
OCEAN.capture.steps.normal.title: 01 Full Render
OCEAN.capture.steps.normal.hint: Complete output, matching what players will actually see.
OCEAN.capture.steps.fresnelHeat.title: 02 Fresnel Heatmap
OCEAN.capture.steps.fresnelHeat.hint: Checks whether flat and steep wave faces reflect differently from the FFT normals.
OCEAN.capture.steps.hdrHeadroom.title: 03 HDR Headroom
OCEAN.capture.steps.hdrHeadroom.hint: Checks whether highlights have energy above 1.0, which later glitter work needs.
OCEAN.capture.steps.baseBody.title: 04 Base Water Body
OCEAN.capture.steps.baseBody.hint: Shows the core water color and dark side depth.
OCEAN.capture.steps.baseColor.title: 05 Base Color Before Foam
OCEAN.capture.steps.baseColor.hint: Shows the base transition before glitter and foam, useful for spotting gray haze.
OCEAN.capture.steps.stage1Base.title: 06 Stage 1 Base Pass
OCEAN.capture.steps.stage1Base.hint: Disables foam, glitter, refraction, and interaction layers, leaving body water plus Fresnel reflection.
OCEAN.capture.steps.cascade0Foam.title: 07 Cascade 0 Raw Fold
OCEAN.capture.steps.cascade0Foam.hint: Stage 2 check: large-cascade ridges should run continuously along the wind, not as salt-grain dots.
OCEAN.capture.steps.cascade1Foam.title: 08 Cascade 1 Raw Fold
OCEAN.capture.steps.cascade1Foam.hint: Stage 2 check: mid-cascade ridges, also expected to chain continuously.
OCEAN.capture.steps.cascade2Foam.title: 09 Cascade 2 Raw Fold
OCEAN.capture.steps.cascade2Foam.hint: Stage 2 check: the high-frequency cascade may be choppier but should still hug crests, not uniform noise.
OCEAN.capture.steps.fftFoam.title: 10 FFT Crest Bands
OCEAN.capture.steps.fftFoam.hint: Stage 2 check: consumer-sharpened fold should read as clear crest ridges.
OCEAN.capture.steps.specBreakup.title: 11 Glitter Breakup
OCEAN.capture.steps.specBreakup.hint: Stage 3 calibration heatmap: micro-facet zones where glints are born. Too dark = window too high (sterile); too bright = carpet.
OCEAN.capture.steps.sssMask.title: 12 Crest SSS
OCEAN.capture.steps.sssMask.hint: Stage 5 calibration: FFT-local crest thinness x backlight, independent from storm swell slopes.
OCEAN.debug.effects.baseWater.label: Base Water / Transparency
OCEAN.debug.effects.baseWater.hint: Show only the base water color and opacity.
OCEAN.debug.effects.canvasRefraction.hin: Sample the scene below the water and distort it with the wave surface.
OCEAN.debug.effects.fresnel.label: Surface Reflection
OCEAN.debug.effects.fresnel.hint: Large-area reflection from the viewing angle of the water.
OCEAN.debug.effects.glitter.label: Glitter Highlights
OCEAN.debug.effects.glitter.hint: The small, constantly shifting specular highlights.
OCEAN.debug.effects.fftWhitecaps.label: FFT Whitecaps
OCEAN.debug.effects.fftWhitecaps.hint: Open-water crest foam; does not affect boat wakes, token wakes, or shore foam.
OCEAN.debug.effects.movingFoam.label: Moving Foam Lines
OCEAN.debug.effects.movingFoam.hint: Small foam streaks that advance with the wind direction.
OCEAN.debug.effects.tokenRipples.label: Token Wakes
OCEAN.debug.effects.tokenRipples.hint: Ripples and foam caused by moving tokens.
OCEAN.debug.effects.foamField.label: Foam Field
OCEAN.debug.effects.foamField.hint: A dynamic foam layer written by FFT crests and interactors; it spreads, drifts with the visible surface flow, and fades over time.
OCEAN.debug.effects.wakeTexture.label: Wake Foam Texture
OCEAN.debug.effects.wakeTexture.hint: Use foam and turbulence textures to break up wake highlights; disable to fall back to procedural noise.
OCEAN.tune.title: Ocean Tuning
OCEAN.tune.exported: Current values were printed to the F12 console.
OCEAN.control.title: Ocean Control
OCEAN.control.fav.empty: No favorites yet — tap the star key, then favorite parameters in any category.
OCEAN.control.fav.addHint: Tap the star on a parameter to add it to Favorites on the home page.
OCEAN.control.search.empty: No matching parameters. Search by label or uniform name.
OCEAN.control.level.toggle: Move this item between Basic and Advanced
OCEAN.control.edit.toggle: Edit mode: organize Favorites and Basic / Advanced
OCEAN.control.edit.hint: Edit mode: ★ adds / removes a parameter from Favorites; tap the Basic / Advanced tag to move it between the two layers.
OCEAN.control.export.title: Export all current settings to the console (F12) to bake into a preset
OCEAN.control.preset.add: Save current settings as a new water style
OCEAN.control.preset.namePlaceholder: Name the new style, e.g. Shallow green
OCEAN.control.idle.addHint: Tap the archive key to move a parameter into Idle (hidden from this category); reopen Idle and tap again to restore.
OCEAN.control.idle.note: These items are disabled or for development diagnostics only — usually unused in production, and dragging them mostly has no visible effect. Kept here for review; safe to clean up once confirmed.
OCEAN.onboarding.title: Ocean Quick Start
OCEAN.onboarding.body: These are the essential controls for regular water and Ocean travel.
OCEAN.onboarding.region.title: Water in Regular Scenes
OCEAN.onboarding.travel.title: Ocean Travel Scenes
OCEAN.onboarding.client.title: Dependency and Personal Quality
OCEAN.onboarding.warmupNote: The first Ocean Region initializes water shaders, FFT waves, and the Region soft mask, so the canvas may pause briefly. Creating more water in the same scene is usually faster.
OCEAN.onboarding.stepPanel: Click the Ocean icon in the left toolbar to open the control panel.
OCEAN.onboarding.stepRegion: Create ocean water by drawing a Region: outline the water area with Foundry Regions, then add the Ocean Water behavior to that Region.
OCEAN.onboarding.travel.convert: Right-click the target Scene in Scene Navigation or the Scenes Directory. Choose full-screen Ocean travel, or replace only the Scene background and keep Foundry Canvas features such as tokens, walls, lights, and the grid.
OCEAN.onboarding.travel.restore: Right-click an active travel Scene to switch to the other Ocean mode or restore it as a regular Scene. Its travel settings remain stored.
OCEAN.onboarding.scenic3d: Scenic3D supplies the 3D ship library and shared ship picker, so Ocean requires it. Scenic3D does not render the travel ocean.
OCEAN.onboarding.quality: Each player can open Game Settings → Configure Settings → Module Settings → 3D Sea Travel Settings and choose Low, Medium, or High for this device.
OCEAN.travel.convertedCanvasBackground: Ocean now replaces the background of {name}. The original background path is unchanged.
OCEAN.travel.restored: Restored {name} as a regular scene. Its travel settings remain in the Scene data.
OCEAN.travel.loadingEnvironment: Preparing the sky and open water
OCEAN.travel.loadingShipDetail: The new ship will replace the current one when ready
OCEAN.travel.startFailed: Ocean travel scene failed to start: {message}
OCEAN.travel.contextLost: The Ocean travel graphics context was interrupted. The Foundry board is visible again.
OCEAN.travel.timeFailed: Ocean travel cannot currently synchronize server time.
OCEAN.travel.shipFailed: The selected travel ship failed to load; the previous ship remains active: {message}
OCEAN.travel.saveFailed: Could not save travel scene settings: {message}
OCEAN.travel.redrawFailed: Could not redraw the restored regular scene: {message}
OCEAN.travel.fullscreenSceneHint: The full-screen ocean covers tokens, tiles, walls, lights, and Regions, so use a dedicated empty Scene. Foundry's left tools remain available.
OCEAN.travel.canvasBackgroundSceneHint: Ocean only replaces the background at runtime; the Scene background path is unchanged. Foundry still draws tokens, tiles, walls, lights, the grid, and Regions.
OCEAN.travel.notTravelScene: The current Scene is not an Ocean travel scene.
OCEAN.travel.playerDefaultsFullscreenHin: The GM sets world defaults here. Each player can override quality and mouse parallax in 3D Sea Travel Settings.
OCEAN.travel.playerDefaultsCanvasHint: Canvas background mode always drives parallax from canvas movement. Each player can still override quality.
OCEAN.travel.canvasPanParallaxHint: Dragging or panning the Foundry canvas moves the Ocean camera. Pointer position no longer drives parallax.
OCEAN.travel.ambienceHint: The GM controls playback for every client. Each player still sets the actual level with Foundry's Environment volume.
OCEAN.travel.presetLimit: You can save up to 64 travel presets.
OCEAN.travel.defaultsRestored: Defaults restored. The prior state was saved as a recoverable preset.
OCEAN.travel.cameraHint.cinematic: A low rear-quarter shot with the ocean filling most of the frame.
OCEAN.travel.cameraHint.stern: Centers the stern and the wake stretching into the distance.
OCEAN.travel.cameraHint.broadside: Shows the full ship profile against the scale of the sea.
OCEAN.travel.cameraHint.lead: Looks back from ahead as the bow meets the waves.
OCEAN.travel.shipPickerFailed: Could not open the travel ship picker: {message}
OCEAN.travel.hints.seabirdFrequency: 0 disables all seabirds; 1 is normal and 3 is most frequent. Drag to preview and release to share with players. Flight speed stays the same.
OCEAN.travel.hints.quality: Affects only this client's performance and clarity; it is not synchronized.
OCEAN.travel.hints.modelId: Stored on this travel scene; switching preserves voyage progress, camera, and time of day. High-poly ships use simplified geometry on Low/Medium and retain the original mesh on High/Ultra.
OCEAN.travel.hints.scale: Scales the ship, draft footprint, motion, and wake together. The current ship reloads smoothly without resetting voyage progress.
OCEAN.travel.hints.seaState: Sets the baseline wave spectrum and overall sea behavior.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waveHeight: Adjusts total significant wave height without changing the wind-sea and swell energy split.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waveBodyScale: Adjusts peak periods and crest spacing; higher values produce longer, slower wave bodies.
OCEAN.travel.hints.swellMix: Moves energy from short-period wind waves into long-period swell while keeping total wave height fixed.
OCEAN.travel.hints.choppiness: Controls how sharp and forward-leaning crests become.
OCEAN.travel.hints.foam: Adjusts whitecaps and surface foam coverage.
OCEAN.travel.hints.motionSpeed: Synchronizes ship, waves, and travel-camera progression speed.
OCEAN.travel.hints.engineMode: FFT is the production path; switching engines rebuilds the wave field.
OCEAN.travel.hints.cameraWaveFollow: Controls how much the travel camera follows the local long-wave mean; zero keeps world height fixed and one fully follows it.
OCEAN.travel.hints.timeMode: Clock mode runs the full day cycle; manual mode directly controls sun direction.
OCEAN.travel.hints.clockHours: Every client continues from this time using the server clock.
OCEAN.travel.hints.celestialTimeScale: Game hours advanced per real second; zero pauses the sky.
OCEAN.travel.hints.sunAzimuthOffset: Rotates sun and moon azimuth without changing their height for the current time.
OCEAN.travel.hints.sunAzimuth: Sun direction around the horizon in manual mode.
OCEAN.travel.hints.sunElevation: Sun height above the horizon in manual mode.
OCEAN.travel.hints.moonPhase: Zero and one are new moon; 0.5 is full moon.
OCEAN.travel.hints.cloudMode: Volumetric clouds look best; lightweight clouds suit slower hardware.
OCEAN.travel.hints.cloudCoverage: Controls how much of the sky is covered by clouds.
OCEAN.travel.hints.cloudDensity: Controls internal cloud thickness and light blocking.
OCEAN.travel.hints.atmosphere: Controls humid marine haze and distant scattering.
OCEAN.travel.hints.exposure: Adjusts base camera exposure; the day-cycle adaptation remains active.
OCEAN.travel.hints.type: Open ocean omits the bottom; Bahama Bank keeps shallow cyan water near the viewer and deepens toward the horizon.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waterMedium: Writes the medium, clarity, three tones, saturation, brightness, and contrast into the same advanced controls.
OCEAN.travel.hints.clarity: Adjusts particle scattering without fading the water color as plain opacity.
OCEAN.travel.hints.shoalAccent: Strengthens turquoise crests and shoals while remaining driven by current light.
OCEAN.travel.hints.bankWorldScale: World-space coverage scale of the shoal field.
OCEAN.travel.hints.shoalNearCoverage: Sets how much near-screen water stays at the main shallow depth without drifting as the ship travels.
OCEAN.travel.hints.shoalTransitionWidth: Sets the width of the fade from turquoise foreground water to deep blue near the horizon.
OCEAN.travel.hints.shallowDepth: Finite water depth across the main shoal.
OCEAN.travel.hints.shoulderDepth: Depth of the transition shoulder before open water.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waterSaturation: Adjusts water-pixel color intensity without changing the sky itself, ships, or foam.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waterBrightness: Adjusts water scattering and bottom return, with a lighter effect on reflected radiance.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waterContrast: Expands or compresses the difference between shadowed and lit water.
OCEAN.travel.hints.foamWhiteness: Adjusts foam albedo without making night foam self-lit.
OCEAN.travel.hints.glitterGain: Controls sun glitter or moonlit silver highlights.
OCEAN.travel.hints.reflectionGain: Adjusts wet-surface reflection from sky and clouds.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waterTint: Controls the base hue of the water body.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waterShadowTint: Controls the hue of backlit water and wave troughs.
OCEAN.travel.hints.waterLightTint: Controls the hue of lit wave faces and shallow return light.
OCEAN.travel.runtimeHint: Camera, preset and ambience changes apply to all players.
OCEAN.travel.editingHint: Changes preview live and save when you release a slider or choose an option.
OCEAN.travel.ambienceVolumeHint: Each player controls the volume in Foundry’s ambience settings.
OCEAN.travel.presetManagementHint: Save the current scene as a preset. Restoring defaults first saves a copy of the current settings.
